subtopic: ONNX / Shape inference — dynamic vs static shapes
learningObjective: Understand ONNX shape inference and how dynamic dimensions are represented in a model.
stem: Which statement about ONNX shape inference and dynamic dimensions is correct?

options.text: ONNX represents dynamic dimensions by encoding a runtime `Tensor<int64>` shape argument as an implicit first input to every op, replacing the static shape annotation.
ONNX shape inference always produces fully static shapes; any op that cannot be statically resolved is deleted from the graph before serialization.
ONNX has no shape inference mechanism; every runtime must implement its own inference from scratch, and the model file never contains any type/shape annotations.

ONNX supports symbolic (named) dynamic dimensions on tensor shapes; `onnx.shape_inference` propagates concrete or symbolic shape/dtype information through the graph where op rules allow it, and unresolved dimensions remain symbolic — consumers use this info for planning but do not require full staticity.

explanation: ONNX supports symbolic dynamic dimensions (named as strings in the `TensorShapeProto`) alongside concrete integers. Shape inference (`onnx.shape_inference`) walks the graph applying op-specific inference rules, propagating shapes and dtypes to intermediate values where possible; unresolved dimensions remain symbolic (or unknown). Consumers use this info for buffer planning, kernel selection, or converting to a downstream compiler that specializes further.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: shape is a metadata annotation on values, not an input-tensor mechanism.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: ONNX does not require full staticity.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: ONNX has a documented shape-inference API and per-op rules.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: named dynamic dims + partial shape inference is the standard ONNX approach.

assumptions: ONNX shape inference API and TensorShapeProto as documented.
nonImplications: Does not imply shape inference solves every case; some ops require constant folding to resolve shapes.
Does not imply symbolic dims are equivalent to concrete dims for all downstream tools.

distractorRationales.B: Wrong claim of fully static requirement.
distractorRationales.C: Wrong claim of no shape-inference API.

sourceRefs.locator: Shape inference API; TensorShapeProto symbolic dimensions
